After a significant personnel shift resulting from the Deferred Resignation Program (DRP), 
USTRANSCOM performed a strategic realignment, transferring overarching Mission Area 
Management responsibilities—specifically the oversight of IT investments—from the COO to 
CFO. This reorganization requires a transition period for the CFO to establish, codify, and 
implement new governance workflows and operational procedures.  For this reason, the 
Government is adding an option period on a sole-source basis to C5T Corporation as a logical 
follow-on to a previous order, in accordance with FAR 16.507-6(b)(3). This regulation permits 
such action in the interest of economy and efficiency when all potential offerors received a fair 
opportunity to compete for the original order. For reasons that follow, C5T is the only capable 
source to meet the immediate needs for continued PfM services.  
 
The 12-month option period allows sufficient time to re-define the scope of the work under the 
new CFO structure, identify areas of responsibility, document all new requirements and 
deliverables, and establish performance metrics in advance of preparing for a new competitive 
solicitation.  This process requires time for impacted personnel to develop a requirements 
package that reflects the new needs.

Award of a contract on a limited sources basis for emergent repair actions required to the Emergency Diesel Engine Scavenging Air Blower on a Los Angeles-class submarine, including providing a detailed repair requirement report and completion of an operational test to validate satisfactory completion of overhaul.

5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority.

The requirement for repair and overhaul was generated after the Emergency Diesel Generator Blower (EDGB) was discovered to be inoperable on 26 January 2026. This date marks the first point at which the government became aware of the deficiency. The need for immediate corrective action therefore did not arise from any government delay, but from an unforeseen equipment failure that directly impacts operational commitments.

The Los Angeles-class submarine is tasked with supporting real world operational commitments. To meet these commitments, the EDGB repair must be completed no later than 31 March 2026. This deadline reflects the submarine's scheduled operational tasking and the minimum time required to restore full emergency power capability.

The EDGB is a critical component of the submarine's emergency power and propulsion support systems. Without a functioning EDGB, the submarine's ability to execute required maneuvers, maintain redundancy in emergency conditions, and meet operational commitments is significantly degraded. Failure to apply urgency to this procurement would therefore jeopardize the operator's ability to meet assigned operational commitments.

representative due to the proprietary equipment, tooling, and technical data involved.
